candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — type 2 diabetes medication selection / metformin teaching
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that contemporary type 2 diabetes pharmacotherapy is individualized rather than governed by a universal metformin-first rule, while recognizing metformin remains a common option when no other factors direct treatment.

options.A: Medication choice is individualized; metformin is commonly used when no other clinical considerations drive the choice, but cardiovascular, kidney, heart-failure, weight, safety, access, and preference factors may favor other or additional agents
options.B: Metformin is mandatory as the first medication for every person with type 2 diabetes before any other glucose-lowering drug can be considered
options.C: Metformin is now reserved only for people who have failed all GLP-1 receptor agonists and SGLT2 inhibitors
options.D: Drug selection in type 2 diabetes is based only on the A1C value and should not consider comorbidities or patient preferences

candidate.rationale: The ADA 2026 Standards recommend a person-centered shared decision-making approach to glucose-lowering therapy. Selection should consider cardiovascular and kidney disease, heart failure, weight goals, hypoglycemia risk, adverse effects, cost/access, treatment burden, and individual preference. Metformin remains effective, inexpensive, widely available, and commonly used when no additional considerations direct therapy, but it is not a universal prerequisite before therapies with proven cardiorenal or other benefits. Therefore A is the best answer.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Current ADA standards use individualized medication selection rather than a universal metformin-first requirement; metformin remains commonly used when no other considerations direct therapy.
candidate.source_document_title: 9. Pharmacologic Approaches to Glycemic Treatment: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
candidate.source_locator: Pharmacologic Therapy for Adults With Type 2 Diabetes, Recommendation 9.5 and 'Choice of Glucose-Lowering Therapy': use person-centered shared decision-making considering cardiovascular, kidney, weight and other comorbidities, hypoglycemia, cost/access, adverse effects and preferences; metformin is commonly used and historically first-line when no additional considerations inform choice beyond glucose lowering
candidate.source_version_date: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Diabetes Care 49(Suppl. 1), published 2026
candidate.stem: A client newly diagnosed with type 2 diabetes asks whether everyone should start metformin as the first medication. Which response by the nurse best reflects current diabetes standards?
